The automobile exception permits warrantless searches of vehicles if there is a reasonable belief that evidence of a crime is present.
The automobile exception is grounded in the mobility of vehicles and the reduced expectation of privacy in automobiles.
The automobile exception does not apply if the connection between the automobile and the contraband is purely coincidental.
An impoundment must be lawful and may raise separate Fourth Amendment concerns.
The absence of any illegal items found during the search may suggest that the search was not justified under the automobile exception.
